tools.name: list_wikis
tools.description: List all available wikis with metadata: slug, title, description, tags, status, last updated, document count, and `scope` (what each wiki covers, what it does NOT cover, and how current it is — use this to pick a wiki and to decide when to fall back to web search). Includes "coming soon" placeholder

tools.name: open_wiki
tools.description: Orient yourself in one wiki, in a single call: returns its metadata, `scope` (coverage / not-covered / freshness), document count, the entry document, and a `map` of all documents (paths + titles, grouped by folder) so you can pick what to read_document next. Use a slug from list_wikis.

tools.name: read_document
tools.description: Read one document in a wiki. Without `section`, returns the full Markdown (frontmatter stripped) plus a provenance footer. tools.description: Find the best-matching PAGES for a query, ranked by how many of your query terms each page covers. Searches one wiki if `wiki` is given, otherwise every active wiki. tools.name: list_skills
tools.description: List the agent skills library: field-tested procedures for specific jobs (e.g. benchmarking a local model, building a browser game, producing a video). Each entry has name, one-line description (when to use it), `access` ("free" or "pro"), `readable` (whether YOU can read it with your current access

tools.name: read_skill
tools.description: Load one skill to follow it. Without `path`, returns its SKILL.md (the procedure itself) plus the list of its other files; pass `path` (e.g. "references/gotchas.md" or "scripts/check.py") to read one of those. If the skill names a backing wiki, use search/read_document on that wiki for current facts

tools.name: list_agent_tools
tools.description: List the command-line tools that ship with the specialist agents (complete agents built for one job, e.g. marketing, video generation, local LLMs). tools.name: read_agent_tool
tools.description: Load one agent tool by name. A "pro" (read-only) tool: its README (what it checks, how to run it) plus its file list. Add `path` to read one listed file, e.g. the source. The tool runs on the user's machine, not here. Before saving, running or scheduling anything from it, show the user what it does

tools.name: list_routines
tools.description: List the routines (scheduled jobs) that ship with the specialist agents: each has a schedule, the `specialist` it comes from, the skills its prompt relies on, and whether it is script only (no agent). `readable` says whether YOU can load it with your current access. Pass `query` to filter by keyword

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.
